name: What is the difference between a detached guest suite and an ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a detached guest suite and an ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: The terms 'detached guest suite' and 'Accessory Dwelling Unit' (ADU) are often used interchangeably, but there can be subtle differences. An ADU is a legally defined, secondary housing unit on a single-family residential lot that provides independent living facilities, including a kitchen and bathroom. A detached guest suite might be less formally defined, sometimes without a full kitchen, primarily for temporary guest accommodation. However, most modern detached guest suites are built to ADU standards to maximize their utility and value.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a legally defined independent living unit with a kitchen, while a guest suite might be less formal. Most modern guest suites are built as ADUs.
